title: validate_session_urls: prefix check allows data:http://... and similar bypasses
description: client.rs validate_session_urls: The check is url.starts_with("http://") || url.starts_with("https://"). A URL like 'https://legit.example.com@evil.example.com/api/' passes this check because it starts with 'https://' but has a user-info component that causes the actual HTTP request to go to evil.example.com. Similarly 'https://evil.example.com/api/?redirect=https://good' is harmless but a URL with embedded newlines would confuse logging. More concretely: a MITM server could return apiUrl: 'https://evil.example.com' and the check passes — but that is actually fine because the URLs are used verbatim by reqwest which parses them correctly. The actual attack vector is url::Url::parse could be used here but is not. The real gap is: the check does not validate that the URL actually parses — a crafted string like 'https://\x00evil.com' starts with https:// but will either cause reqwest to error at request time or produce unexpected behavior. Mitigation: parse each URL with url::Url::parse and re-validate scheme from the parsed result.
